title: What shapes do we get by joining the midpoints of a triangle?
description: An equilateral triangle with side eight centimetres has the midpoints of its sides joined. The video finds the angles and sides of each corner triangle and then of the middle one. Keeko's doubt is that the upside down middle triangle is a different shape.
teaching_notes: One idea: two equal sides around a sixty degree angle make the corner triangle equilateral, and the middle triangle is built from the third sides. Watch for students who think a turned triangle is a different triangle.

source: An equilateral triangle has side 8 cm. Show that joining the
video_script.why: The child needs to see why the first step of the Ruhee Triangle gives four identical triangles.
video_script.substitution: Use the corner triangle's two equal sides and its sixty degree angle to find all its angles and sides.
video_script.anchor: an equilateral triangle of side eight centimetres with its midpoints joined, as in the Ruhee Triangle of the book
video_script.wrong_answer: the middle triangle is a different shape
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the middle triangle is a different shape because it is upside down. Turning a triangle does not change its sides, and its sides are the three third sides of the corner triangles.
video_script.payoff_line: Joining the midpoints makes four equilateral triangles, each with sides of four centimetres

final_answer.value: Four equilateral triangles, each of side 4 cm
final_answer.spoken: four equilateral triangles, each with sides of four centimetres

names.Ruhee: Polish mathematician who discovered the carpet and the triangle

hold_back: Answer: four equilateral triangles, each of side 4 cm
never_show: the middle triangle drawn as a different shape
maths_rules: midpoint of a side of 8 cm: 8 / 2 = 4 cm
corner triangle: two sides of 4 cm with the 60 degree angle between them
angle sum of a triangle: 180 degrees
base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal: (180 - 60) / 2 = 60 degrees
all three angles 60 degrees, so the triangle is equilateral and the third side is 4 cm
middle triangle sides: 4 cm, 4 cm, 4 cm
video_script.design: One big triangle with its midpoints joined; the three corner triangles and the middle one are lit in turn.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; an equilateral triangle with each side marked 8 cm

marks.book: the title card and the triangle appear
marks.join: the midpoints are marked and joined by three lines
marks.ask: the four small triangles are outlined with question marks

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about an equilateral triangle with sides of eight centimetres.
<bookmark mark='join'/>Mark the midpoint of each side and join the three midpoints.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The triangle breaks into four smaller triangles. How do their sizes and shapes compare?

beats.on_screen: the triangle with its four parts stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: each side of the big triangle shows two equal halves; the three corner triangles and the middle triangle are outlined

marks.half: each side splits into two equal halves
marks.corner: the three corner triangles are outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='half'/>A midpoint cuts a side into two equal halves.
<bookmark mark='corner'/>The three triangles at the corners each hold one corner of the big triangle.
<bookmark mark='middle'/>The fourth triangle sits in the middle, between the three joining lines.

beats.on_screen: Given: equilateral triangle, each side 8 cm; midpoints of the sides are joined

marks.given: the side length and the joined midpoints are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, an equilateral triangle has each side eight centimetres, and the midpoints of its sides are joined.

beats.on_screen: To show: the 4 small triangles are identical equilateral triangles

marks.find: the words identical equilateral triangles are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to show that the four small triangles are identical equilateral triangles.

beats.on_screen: Corner triangle: two sides of 8 / 2 = 4 cm, with the 60 degree angle of the big triangle between them

marks.half: 8 / 2 = 4 cm is written on two sides of one corner triangle
marks.angle: the 60 degree angle between them lights up

narration: <bookmark mark='half'/>Step one, take one corner triangle. Two of its sides are halves, and eight divided by two is four centimetres.
<bookmark mark='angle'/>The angle between them is the sixty degree angle of the big triangle.

beats.on_screen: Two equal sides, so isosceles: base angles equal, (180 - 60) / 2 = 60 degrees each

marks.iso: the words two equal sides, so isosceles are written
marks.calc: (180 - 60) / 2 = 60 degrees is written at the two base angles

narration: <bookmark mark='iso'/>Step two, two sides are equal, so the triangle is isosceles and its base angles are equal.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>The angles add up to one hundred and eighty degrees. One hundred and eighty minus sixty, divided by two, is sixty degrees each.

beats.on_screen: All three angles are 60 degrees, so the corner triangle is equilateral and its third side is 4 cm

marks.all: the three angles of 60 degrees are written
marks.third: the third side is marked 4 cm

narration: <bookmark mark='all'/>Step three, all three angles are sixty degrees, so the corner triangle is equilateral.
<bookmark mark='third'/>Its third side is also four centimetres. All three corner triangles are the same.

beats.on_screen: Middle triangle: its sides are the three third sides, 4 cm, 4 cm and 4 cm

marks.sides: the three joining lines are marked 4 cm each
marks.same: all four triangles are shaded the same colour

narration: <bookmark mark='sides'/>Step four, the middle triangle has the three third sides as its sides.
<bookmark mark='same'/>They measure four, four and four centimetres, so it is equilateral and matches the corners.

beats.on_screen: Answer: four equilateral triangles, each of side 4 cm
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Joining the midpoints makes four equilateral triangles, each with sides of four centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the triangle
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble sits beside the upside down middle triangle; the middle triangle is lifted out, turned the right way up and put back

marks.doubt: the bubble appears beside the middle triangle
marks.turn: the middle triangle is lifted out and turned the right way up
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the sides 4 cm each glow

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the middle triangle is a different shape, because it is upside down.
<bookmark mark='turn'/>Turn it the right way up and put it back. Turning does not change the sides.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>We need its sides, not which way up it sits.
